related_questions.question: What is the best treatment for a stroke?
related_questions.snippet: The main treatment for an ischemic stroke is a medicine called tissue plasminogen activator (tPA). It breaks up the blood clots that block blood flow to your brain. A healthcare provider will inject tPA into a vein in your arm. This type of medicine must be given within 3 hours after stroke symptoms start.
related_questions.title: Stroke - Treatment | NHLBI, NIH

related_questions.question: What is the life expectancy of a person after a stroke?
related_questions.snippet: A large 2019 Swedish study including people who survived at least 30 days after a first stroke found a 5-year survival rate of 49.4% for those who had an ischemic stroke. For people who had an intracerebral hemorrhage, the 5-year survival rate was 37.8%. A 2019 German study found similar results after 5 years.
related_questions.title: Outlook and Life Expectancy After a Stroke - Healthline

related_questions.question: What is the most important thing to do after a stroke?
related_questions.snippet: Activities of daily living (ADL) become the focus of rehabilitation after a stroke. ADL typically include tasks like bathing or preparing food. But you should also talk with your care team about activities important to you, such as performing a work-related skill or a hobby, to help set your recovery goals.
related_questions.title: Stroke Recovery Timeline | Johns Hopkins Medicine

related_questions.question: What should be avoided after a mild stroke?
related_questions.snippet: Eat more whole foods; avoid processed foods, sugar and salt; reduce your fat intake; and eat poultry or fish instead of red meat. Care for your mental health.
related_questions.title: Lifestyle Changes After a Stroke | Northwestern Medicine

text_blocks.snippet: Stroke treatment focuses on restoring blood flow to the brain, minimizing damage, and preventing future strokes. Treatment varies depending on the type of stroke (ischemic or hemorrhagic) and the time since onset. Common treatments include medications like tPA for ischemic strokes, surgical interventions, and rehabilitation.
snippet_highlighted_words: medications like tPA for ischemic strokes, surgical interventions, and rehabilitation

list.title: Thrombolytics (clot-busting drugs):
list.snippet: tPA (tissue plasminogen activator) is the most common medication, administered intravenously within a narrow window (usually 3-4.5 hours of symptom onset) to dissolve the clot.

list.title: Mechanical Thrombectomy:
list.snippet: A surgical procedure to remove the clot, often used when tPA is not an option or for larger clots, and may be performed up to 24 hours after the stroke.

list.title: Antiplatelet and Anticoagulant Medications:
list.snippet: These medications help prevent future clots from forming, often used long-term after a stroke.

list.title: Other Medications:
list.snippet: Blood pressure control, seizure prevention, and medications to reduce pressure in the brain may also be used.

list.title: Medications:
list.snippet: Blood pressure control and medications to reverse the effects of blood thinners are often used.

list.title: Surgical Procedures:
list.snippet: Procedures like surgical clipping or endovascular coiling may be used to repair aneurysms or abnormal blood vessels.

list.title: Surgery to Release Blood:
list.snippet: If there's excessive bleeding, surgery may be needed to relieve pressure on the brain.
Physical Therapy: Helps improve mobility, balance, and coordination.
Occupational Therapy: Helps with daily living activities, such as dressing and eating.
Speech Therapy: Helps with communication and swallowing difficulties.

list.title: Time is Critical:
list.snippet: Prompt treatment is crucial for minimizing brain damage and improving outcomes.

list.title: Early Detection:
list.snippet: Recognizing stroke symptoms and calling 911 immediately is essential, according to the Mayo Clinic.

list.title: Stroke Centers:
list.snippet: Specialized stroke centers have the expertise and resources to provide comprehensive stroke care.
